title: Signal curation sprint canvas + compact metrics glossary
content:
Purpose:
Compact reference and working canvas for a 2-week sprint to: 1) prune low-value signals, 2) standardize metric definitions for inference runtime and KV cache indicators, 3) prototype three microdash templates and one operator investigation flow.

Background / motivation:
We have a large backlog of panel widgets and instrumented signals. Many dashboards are noisy or expensive to query. This doc attempts a lightweight, operational-first approach: define a small canonical glossary of metrics for token serving + KV/cache behavior, attach owners, and describe minimal trace/span conventions to make trace linking reliable during incidents. The goal of the sprint is not full instrumentation parity but to create repeatable templates and ownership so future signals are easier to evaluate.

Sprint goals (2 weeks):
- Ship a 3-panel microdash template: Latency attribution, KV-warmth & eviction heatmap, and Failure-mode ladder.
- Reduce active dashboard panels by 15% (sunsetting low-value tiles).
- Implement revised metric definitions for 8 core signals and publish glossary.
- Add trace span annotations for prefix-warmup and fallback routes (spec + 1 PR).
- Run one tabletop with SRE + Runtime team to validate investigation flow.

Acceptance criteria:
- Microdash template stored in dashboard repo and annotated with query cost estimates.
- All 8 metrics have owner and dataset mapping (metric -> source -> sample rate).
- Sampling budget defined and enforced via sampling policy in tracing service.
- Tabletop run with notes / action items logged in linked Jira (OBS-512).

Compact metrics glossary (canonical 8 core signals):
1) ttf-token (unit: ms, agg: p50/p95/p99)
   - description: Time from server receive to first token emitted to client for generation requests.
   - owner: Marc Liu
   - source: inference_runtime/latency_first_token
   - sample policy: full for canary tenants, 1% for regular; record session id for trace stitching.
   - alert hint: sustained p95 > 300ms for >5min.

2) kv-warmth (unit: fraction 0-1, agg: p50/p90)
   - description: Fraction of requests that hit prefix/KV cache for the primary model shard.
   - owner: Sofia Patel
   - source: kvcache/serve/hit_rate
   - sample policy: aggregated counters (no tracing).
   - alert hint: drop >10% absolute over 15min combined with ttf-token regressions.

3) kv-eviction-rate (unit: evictions/min, agg: rate)
   - description: Evictions observed per minute on model shard KV store. Correlate to tail latency.
   - owner: Jonah Reyes
   - source: kvcache/evictions
   - sample policy: aggregated.

4) continuous-batch-size (unit: items, agg: avg/p90)
   - description: Effective batch size used by continuous batching during steady state.
   - owner: Priya Nambiar
   - source: runtime/batching/observed_batch_size
   - sample policy: sample every minute.

5) fallback-rate (unit: fraction, agg: 1h rate)
   - description: Fraction of requests that were routed to fallback model/variant due to capacity or error.
   - owner: Aisha Gomez
   - source: routing/fallbacks/counts
   - sample policy: full counters with tenant dimension.

6) token-error-rate (unit: errors per 10k tokens, agg: rate)
   - description: Token generation errors (model OOM, runtime exceptions) normalized by token output.
   - owner: SRE team (ops-oncall)
   - source: runtime/errors/token_errors
   - sample policy: full for error traces, aggregated counters for alerting.

7) session-kv-latency (unit: ms, agg: p50/p95)
   - description: Latency to retrieve prefix/KV entries for a session query (network+lookups).
   - owner: Infrastructure / KV team
   - source: kvcache/latency
   - sample policy: sample 5% of sessions for traces.

8) cost-per-token-estimate (unit: USD/token_est, agg: avg)
   - description: Derived estimate combining GPU-time, batch size, and token count; used for quick regression detection.
   - owner: Finance + Runtime
   - source: billing/estimates + runtime/telemetry join
   - sample policy: daily aggregation, per-route breakdown.

Tracing conventions (lightweight + investigation-friendly):
- Span naming: <service>.<operation>.<phase> e.g., runtime.generate.first_token, kvcache.fetch.session_prefetch, router.route.fallback
- Trace tags to include: tenant_id, route, model_version, session_id, batch_id, probe=true/false
- Prefix-warmup annotation: when a request triggers KV prefetch, emit span tag kv_prefetch=true and annotate upstream request id.
- Sampling budget: 2M traces/day global cap. Assignment: canaries + debug=true requests = full capture; error-level spans (status>=500) capture full; otherwise probabilistic by tenant (1% standard, configurable).
- Trace retention tiers: incident traces (error/high-rr) retained 90 days, standard sampled retained 30 days.

Dashboard proposals (3 microdash templates):
1) Latency attribution microdash (3 tiles):
   - Tile A: ttf-token p50/p95/p99 with annotations for deployment rollouts.
   - Tile B: stack breakdown by stage (router, prefix-lookup, compilation, kernel_exec) — approximate via derived spans.
   - Tile C: correlated kv-warmth and session-kv-latency heatmap (multi-tenant slicer).
   - Notes: queries must include tenant sampling to keep query cost bounded.

2) KV warmth & eviction heatmap (2 tiles + drilldown):
   - Tile A: per-shard kv-warmth trend (hourly buckets) with eviction overlay.
   - Tile B: eviction-rate distribution histogram by model shard.
   - Drilldown: sample session traces for top evaporation events.

3) Failure-mode ladder (3 tiles):
   - Tile A: token-error-rate trend; Tile B: fallback-rate by route; Tile C: top 5 error messages with example snippet (de-identified).

Investigation flow (operator playbook sketch):
1) Alert fires (e.g., ttf-token p95 > threshold).
2) Open microdash, inspect latency attribution tile. If kv-warmth drop correlates, jump to KV heatmap.
3) If fallback-rate increased, check routing logs and rollout notes.
4) Trigger trace replay for representative sessions (use session id from alert).
5) If not resolvable in 15 min, escalate to runtime oncall, attach trace link + microdash snapshot.

Low-cost instrumentation rules:
- Avoid high-cardinality tags in default dashboards (tenant_id only on drilldowns).
- Aggregate at the earliest stage (service emits p50/p90 counters rather than raw latencies where feasible).
- Use pre-computed rollups for 1h/6h/24h windows to support UI.

Tasks & owners (first-pass):
- T1: Implement metric schema updates for 8 core signals (Marc + Sofia) — PR to metrics repo.
- T2: Create microdash templates and add to dashboard-playbook (Aisha + Jonah).
- T3: Trace sampling policy config + infra constraints (Priya + infra team).
- T4: Tabletop run and notes (SRE lead + product) — schedule week 2.
- T5: Sunset candidate panels list (scrub by owners, due EOD sprint end).

Open questions / risks:
- Cost model for trace retention — finance needs clearer projection before increasing default sample rate.
- How to surface tenant-level kv-warmth without violating privacy / PII policies? Need legal check but propose hashed tenant ids for drilldowns.
- Are there downstream consumers that depend on any of the panels we plan to remove? We need a short deprecation notice flow.

Quick todo (next 48h):
- Lock owners for metrics (Marc to confirm), create Jira sub-tasks under OBS-512.
- Prototype microdash wireframe (Aisha), share with SRE for feedback.
- Draft trace sampling budget note and send to infra mailing list (Priya).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider an "operator mini-story" ribbon at the top of each microdash showing the likely next step (kv -> trace -> routing).
- When instrumenting kv-warmth, add a low-cost moving-average counter to surface sudden drops without full histogram queries.
- Keep the first rollout conservative: only instrument high-traffic model shards and canary tenants for full tracing.

References / links in flight:
- Confluence: Signal Garden Overview (linked_artifacts)
- Jira: OBS-512 (tabletop + tasks)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/432

Last notes:
This is intentionally compact — the goal is to create something operator-first that can be iterated. Be ruthless about removing panels that add noise and not signal. If we can get the three microdash templates and metric owners locked in this sprint, we can evangelize the pattern to product and private deployments next quarter.
